tagline: A spotted dragon drifting through the kelp
summary: Also called the common seadragon, this slender relative of seahorses lives on kelp reefs and seagrass beds along southern Australia. Its reddish body is sprinkled with yellow spots and trimmed with small leafy flaps, and — as with all seadragons — the male carries the eggs.

stats.size: Commonly about 30 cm; up to 45 cm
stats.range: Southern Australia, from about Newcastle (NSW) to Tasmania and west to about Geraldton (WA)

facts.title: Father as nursery
facts.text: Males carry and nourish up to 250 developing eggs on a special patch on the underside of the tail, and some raise two broods in a breeding season.

facts.title: Stealthy hunter
facts.text: Seadragons are ambush predators: relying on camouflage and slow, stealthy approach, they suck up mysids and other tiny crustaceans through a long, tube-like snout.

facts.title: Homebodies
facts.text: Seadragons are a little more mobile than seahorses, yet tend to stay within a home range of roughly 500 m throughout their lives.

facts.title: Victoria's sea emblem
facts.text: The weedy (common) seadragon is the official marine emblem of the Australian state of Victoria.

facts.title: A worrying trend?
facts.text: Citizen-science dive surveys suggested a 59% population decline between 2011 and 2021, and the species is now listed as Vulnerable — though some researchers argue the data are too sparse to be sure of the trend.
